x: We actually started two full teams and a depleted third and our "A" Team of James, Hall, Checkley and Newson were 3rd to Highgate with 38 points.
Congratulations to Eric Hall on once again winning the Civil Service 7 Miles Championship and George Checkley on his 2nd place in the Police 7 miles championship.

We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.

George Checkley however, who seems to relish such conditions, had moved into an early lead in front of our second man Bob Newson, with Norman Guilmant also moving strongly and it looked rosy at halfway.

After some early dashes to the front, a group, including Checkley and Newson, settled down in the lead. George Checkley walked really well to win in 40m.12s. with Bob Newson second, Syd James (whom we are pleased to see out again) third and Eric Froude, still improving, fourth.
Ted Smith was our first man home in (10th) followed by McMullen, Checkley and Newson, 12th, 15th and 16th. We thus finished 2nd in the Scratch Race despite not having our 2 Olympic men.
Ted Smith,showing his true form,was 4th,Syd James 12th, Checkley 5th.McMullen 7th and Newson 13th.After this we can hope to regain the Berman Cup in our own Open on Nov24th.

In the'Middlesex' at Regents Park, our Cadogan A.C. team finished 5th. Cameron, Checkley & L. Jones finishing 16th, 18th and 19th respectively.

As a result the two Georges, Checkley and Beecham, gained international vests. Earlier in the year the runners had finished third in the Brighton relay and the Polytechnic marathon where the team included two of the editing trio.
